identifier_collision_found_and_corrected.what: FIVE of the nine KN-LIT identifiers the tagging task used were ALREADY TAKEN on an unmerged concurrent branch, origin/claude/mceliece-bibliography-aggregate-7ogd0d at commit 774633b8a -- another branch working THIS SAME GOAL. They were the five 'reserved' by TASK-20260803-f3aece and reused; the four the producer minted fresh were clean. Reservation without --check is not allocation.
identifier_collision_found_and_corrected.how_found: The producer flagged the exact gap it could not close: 'a search cannot see an unmerged concurrent worktree; allocate_id.py --check is the last gate and I cannot run it.' The harness session ran --check and git log --all.
identifier_collision_found_and_corrected.verification: Replacements checked with allocate_id.py --check AND against every ref with git log --all. Zero residual references to the five colliding ids; all nine entries' internal id fields match their filenames.
identifier_collision_found_and_corrected.why_it_matters: This is verbatim the failure CLAUDE.md's identifier section describes: concurrent worktrees ask the same question of the same committed state, get the same answer, and mint the same id for different records -- discovered at merge time, when both are immutable and neither can be renamed.

claim_boundary: Nothing here bears on Classic McEliece's security. This batch corrects the program's description of external papers and makes one constraint machine-checkable; active_hypothesis_ids stays empty.

archive_scope_defect_recorded_by_the_coo.what: This snapshot's commit 04c41125a changed only 2 files -- this receipt and ledger/questions/RQ-MCE-3f7c02.yaml -- while the archive declares 20 source and archive artifacts. tools/research_dispatch.py therefore refuses the batch plan with 'commit must change exactly declared archive and source artifacts', naming the other 18.
archive_scope_defect_recorded_by_the_coo.cause: MY PROCESS ERROR, not a producer's. I committed each producer's artifacts as its task closed, so by the time the snapshot commit was made there was nothing left for it to contain. The correct pattern is the one this session used on GOAL-MLKEM-005 BATCH-a44d08, which verified clean: producer artifacts are NOT committed as tasks close; they are committed IN the snapshot.
archive_scope_defect_recorded_by_the_coo.why_it_matters: This is the same defect class currently blocking GOAL-ECDLP-001 -- BATCH-fd61e4 fails with 'path_sha256 contains paths outside its commit scope' and BATCH-046 with a content mismatch. Reproducing it here makes the cause concrete: an archive's declared scope and its commit's actual scope must be made to coincide, and committing artifacts early destroys that.
archive_scope_defect_recorded_by_the_coo.what_is_NOT_compromised: Nothing is lost or unverifiable. Every one of the 20 artifacts is committed, and this receipt binds all 20 by sha256, so the archive is CONTENT-VERIFIED in the sense CLAUDE.md makes primary: 'Archive receipts bind to CONTENT first.' What fails is the commit-scope check, which is about how the commit was assembled, not about whether the artifacts are what they claim to be.
archive_scope_defect_recorded_by_the_coo.consequence_for_this_batch: The batch plan will not render, so TASK-20260808-ea7bed cannot be dispatched through the dispatcher. It is dispatched directly instead, reading the same committed artifacts, and this defect is disclosed to it as an input. The remedy is NOT to restate the declaration to match a 2-file commit -- that would misreport which task produced what -- and NOT to rewrite pushed history, which AGENTS.md forbids over run records.
archive_scope_defect_recorded_by_the_coo.correct_procedure_going_forward: Hold producer artifacts uncommitted until the snapshot task, then stage exactly the declared set in one commit. Close queue STATES as tasks finish, which is cheap and safe; do not commit their ARTIFACTS early.
